title: Autonomous pricepoint batcher and quant-profile merge tooling
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: We need a conservative, tenant-safe autopilot that seeds batch shapes and selects quantization profiles by pricepoint targets (unit-econ first) rather than purely latency thresholds. This PR introduces a two-part system: (1) a pricepoint-driven batch seeder that produces conservative micro-batches and fallback ramp rules, and (2) a quant-profile stitcher that merges candidate quantization profiles from tenant telemetry with safety heuristics to produce deployable presets. The goal is to reduce token cost by ~8-14% for long-tail workloads while maintaining 99th-percentile latency SLOs for premium tenants.

What this PR contains (high level): added core runtime integration (pricepoint scoring and seeding), a lightweight CLI for dry-run simulation, integration tests and e2e synthetic workloads for cost/latency verification, operator docs and a default safe preset for Hosted and Dedicated deployments. It also includes a small operator-visible metric set to track pricepoint conversions and profile-rollout rejections.

Design notes: The batcher runs as a sidecar evaluation loop in the allocator and produces an ordered list of candidate batch shapes with attached safety scores. The quant-profile stitcher consumes profile candidates (observed quantization candidates + curated profiles) and attempts to find the highest-compression profile that passes a simulated quality gate (internal evals against representative prompt sets). We intentionally bias the stitcher toward conservative fallbacks when tests show >1.0% generation divergence or when tail latency risks are non-trivial. The stitcher emits a versioned preset that can be pinned per-tenant.

Config knobs: pricepoint.target_usd_per_1k_tokens (default: 0.75), seed.min_microbatch_qps (default: 5), stitcher.max_allowed_quality_drift_pct (default: 1.0), dry_run=true/false. These values are additive defaults; tenant overrides are allowed via tenant-policy manifests.

Safety and rollout: This implements a staged rollout: dry-run simulation -> canary (1% of traffic) -> gradual ramp (1%->10%->100%) with auto-rollback thresholds tied to unit-econ and latency regressions. A new metric (econ.stitcher_rollout_reject) records candidate rejections and reasons. The PR wires the rollout controller to the existing rollout service and adds a 'force-safe' toggle for immediate operator rollback.

Testing and verification: added unit tests for pricepoint scoring, integration tests for seeding logic (simulated traffic), and e2e scripts that run against the benchmark-lab harness. Benchmarks show a median cost reduction of 9.6% on the seed cohort and no statistically significant change in p95 latency under the benchmark-lab synthetic mixes.

Backward compatibility: no breaking API changes to the public Redwood API. Admin/operator components add new API endpoints under /internal/econ for promo/dry-run controls; these are guarded by RBAC.

Docs: ops guide and quickstart for enabling the feature, explanation of safety gates and how to interpret rollout metrics.

Checklist: - [x] Core runtime batching logic implemented - [x] Quant stitcher and profile merger implemented - [x] Unit/integration/e2e tests added - [x] Docs and quickstart added - [x] Smoke benchmarks run and numbers captured - [x] RBAC controls wired

References: Linear ENG-4123 for orchestration work; SUP-7821 was the customer escalation that drove the conservative default approach.

Notes for reviewers: focus on safety logic in stitcher/simulator (stitcher/simulate.go), rollout integration (rollouts/controller.go), and the set of default knobs in config/econ_defaults.yaml. The dry-run CLI (tools/econctl) intentionally mirrors the operator API to make simulation reproducible.

review_comments: Arjun Patel (2026-02-15): The simulated quality gate is critical -- can you explain the choice of 1.0% drift as default? What happens if the evaluation dataset drifts from production?

Maya Chen (2026-02-15): We chose 1.0% as a conservative starting point after A/B sims; stitcher logs dataset drift and if drift_detected -> it widens filter and forces fallback to curated profiles. We also added a telemetry alarm if drift > 3% over a 24h window.
Lena Ortiz (2026-02-16): Tests look good. Suggest adding an explicit smoke test that verifies the rollback happens when p95 latency increases by >10%.

Maya Chen (2026-02-16): Added smoke e2e that injects latency and verifies controller triggers rollback (see tests/e2e/rollback_smoke.go), and wired the metric econ.rollout_latency_alert for the alerting rule.
Samir Gupta (2026-02-18): Can the stitcher accidentally produce a profile that is not compatible with some quant runtime kernels? Need a compatibility filter before emitting presets.
Maya Chen (2026-02-18): Good catch. Added compatibility checks and a conservative 'kernel_compat' flag; incompatible candidates are rejected and reasoned in rollout logs.
